title: Free-to-play with cosmetics or a paid game? Looking for advice for my co-op action RPG
author: WayOfTheKunai
selftext:
Hey everyone! I'm working on my first game, a 3D online co-op ninja action RPG in Unity, still early in development.



I'm trying to decide on the business model now, since it affects how I design progression and servers:



\*\*Option A: Free-to-play\*\*

\- Free to download

\- In-game currency earned just by playing

\- Real-money purchases only for cosmetic skins (no pay-to-win)



\*\*Option B: Paid (premium)\*\*

\- One-time price

\- Maybe optional cosmetic DLC later



A few things I'm unsure about:

1. For a small indie co-op game, is F2P realistic, or does it only work with a big player base?

2. Does a price tag hurt co-op games, since every friend has to buy it too?

3. How do F2P games do on Steam (visibility, reviews) compared to paid ones?

4. I'm hosting my own servers. Does that push you toward one model or the other?



If you've shipped with either model, I'd love to hear what worked and what you'd do differently. Thanks!

  
i made my game with AI

comments.author: novashiftinteractVN
comments.body:
1. I have not experience about which option is better but in my opinion if the game is not online (like wow, league of legends, fornite etc) I think that cosmetics are not a good way to earn money, if you game is only a co-op experience you should sell it (some examples are the "We were here" games)  
  
2. You may give an extra key for each buy (I saw many games doing that, a friend bought Dont Starve Together and he received an extra key and he gifted it to me. 

3. Probably marketing on social media, shorts in youtube, instagram, tiktok etc

4. It depends on how much money you spend in the server maintenance.

replies.author: WayOfTheKunai
replies.body: Really appreciate you breaking it down point by point, it gave me a much clearer picture of where to go next. Thanks again!

comments.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
comments.body: People aren’t going to pay for cosmetic skins in a non-multiplayer game. The free to play model really only works for very specific kinds of games.

replies.author: WayOfTheKunai
replies.body:
Thanks for the reply! I should have been clearer in my post. It's actually an online multiplayer RPG (MMO-style) with a ninja theme, not just a co-op experience. That's why I'm considering free-to-play, with a battle pass and gold coins that players can spend on cosmetics.

I'm still torn between that and a paid model, though. Since the game is always online, do you think F2P could work here, or would you still go with paid?

comments.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
comments.body: Free to play would work if u add more story content over time as paid dlc, depending on the style the game uses for cosmetics it could work but depends on players, it's made with ai so I recommend disclosing it and as free to play it will attract some players if it catches their eyes, do bear in mind that steam handles the views ur game gets and that not disclosing it will cost ya paying customers, steams refund policy is quite bad for any game in the market but showing players what u can do with ai will get the playerbase.

replies.author: WayOfTheKunai
replies.body: Good call, I'll make sure to clearly disclose it on the store page. The idea of releasing new story chapters as paid DLC is something I hadn't considered, definitely adding that to my notes. Thanks!

replies.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
replies.body: The players that do enjoy ur game will pay for dlc story and stuff, even if u want to do both paid and free to play just limit the free to play severely compared to the paid version, a light version and full game version, the light version only gets a few things from the story and possible small number of dungeons while the full game gets everything.. either way u go about doing it is fine but the light version could offer dlc content that can unlock other features only available in full game and bring it to light version etc.. any way u want to do it

replies.author: WayOfTheKunai
replies.body: That's a really practical middle ground, it lowers the barrier for new players without giving everything away. Gives me a lot to think about while I keep building. Appreciate all the input!

comments.author: No-Pollution7797
comments.body:
Since you're hosting your own servers, I'd lean paid, at least to start. With F2P the server bill grows with every player while only a small slice of them ever buys a skin, and cosmetics mostly sell once there are enough people around to show them off to. Going free later is easy, going from free to paid basically isn't.



For the "every friend has to buy it" worry, a friend pass is worth a look. One owner hosts and can invite friends who haven't bought it, the way Split Fiction did it, so the co-op barrier drops without giving the whole game away.

replies.author: WayOfTheKunai
replies.body: This is probably the clearest breakdown I've gotten so far, really appreciate you taking the time. The server cost angle is something I hadn't fully thought through, and I'm definitely leaning toward paid now.

replies.author: No-Pollution7797
replies.body: Makes sense. If you go paid, a short free demo of the first mission or two does a lot of what F2P would, since people can try it with a friend before either of them buys.
